## Identify the base {#brackets}

Circle the base carrying the exponent. A coefficient outside that base stays in place.

:::::: {.example-pair}

::::: {.model}

<h3>Worked example</h3>

$3x^{-2}\quad\text{and}\quad(3x)^{-2}$

::: {.fragment}

[The exponent belongs to x.]{.annotation}

$3x^{-2}=3\cdot\dfrac{1}{x^2}=\dfrac{3}{x^2}$

:::

::: {.fragment}

[The brackets make 3x the base.]{.annotation}

$(3x)^{-2}=\dfrac{1}{(3x)^2}=\dfrac{1}{9x^2}$

:::

:::::

::::: {.paper}

::: {.fragment}

<h3>Your turn</h3>

$2y^{-3}\quad\text{and}\quad(2y)^{-3}$

Try it on paper, then select **Next** to check.

:::

::: {.fragment}

[Check your working]{.annotation}

$2y^{-3}=\dfrac{2}{y^3}$

$(2y)^{-3}=\dfrac{1}{(2y)^3}=\dfrac{1}{8y^3}$

:::
